assignment: Write the board decision memo for a neighborhood repair cooperative deciding its next six-month opening schedule. Last quarter: Tue noon 122 visits, Thu evening 178, Sat morning 243. Of 84 surveyed members, 35 wanted Sundays and 31 wanted weekday evenings; multiple answers allowed. The lease allows four opening days. Two volunteer captains can each cover one extra shift a fortnight; the paid coordinator already works 32 hours. A Sunday trial would cost 140 currency units per session. Budget for a trial: 1,200. Twelve partner referrals arrived when the shop was closed; time of arrival wasn't recorded. The board wants a decision it can take this month and a way to tell whether access actually improves.

Prepare a decision paper for a city youth orchestra revising its instrument loan program. There are 75 instruments, 62 out on loan, 14 applicants waiting, and 9 instruments due for repair. Sibling sharing is allowed and poorly recorded. Last term 6 instruments returned late; 4 families had outdated contact details. Average repair bill 90 currency units. A sponsor offers 3,000 for one year but bars spending on deposits. Teachers disagree over refundable deposits versus a no-deposit trial. Rehearsals start in six weeks. Write for a board including parents and finance volunteers. Distinguish choices that affect access from choices that affect recovery and repair.

Develop a service design proposal for a small local-history archive moving from ad hoc walk-ins to a reservable study room. One staff member, two desks, a shared magnifier, no public Wi-Fi. Researchers include school groups, family historians and people who cannot use online forms. Twenty percent of requests arrive without a catalog reference. Staff cannot promise that an item is usable until its condition has been checked. A 10-week pilot can use paper, telephone and the existing web form; no new software procurement. Give the director and front-desk team enough detail to pilot it, including a difficult user journey and what they should learn.

Design the wayfinding and information service for a monthly evening market in a former train yard. Entrance north is step-free, entrance east has stairs, and the west gate is for deliveries until 18:30. Performances move indoors in rain, while most stalls stay outside. The event runs 17:00–21:00, permits only freestanding signs, and has one public address speaker near the stage. Volunteer turnover is high. The organizers can print 24 reusable sign panels and one paper handout; mobile reception is unreliable. Produce a design proposal that a printer, a volunteer lead and an accessibility reviewer can use for the first two market nights.

Write an operational analysis for the managers of three fictional branches of a tool library. In April, Harbor logged 510 loans, 48 overdue notices, 12 finally overdue items, and 7 days with a scanner outage. Hill logged 320, 19, 13, and 0. Park logged 400, 36, 16, and 3. In May, Harbor logged 540, 28, 14, and 1; Hill 300, 20, 11, and 0; Park 430, 22, 15, and 0. Notice totals count notifications; finally overdue items are unique and assessed after the manual reconciliation. Loans are transactions. At the beginning of May a reminder text was piloted only at Harbor. Managers want to know what changed, what they can attribute to reminders, and what records to collect next. Use the figures and give a recommendation.

Write a planning analysis for a fictional community cinema choosing whether to expand its annual pass. Four pilot months, Jan through Apr. Passes active: 80, 95, 105, 112. Pass-holder visits: 180, 250, 205, 280. Single tickets sold: 940, 880, 1020, 865. Available seats: 2000, 1840, 2100, 1750. Single ticket 9 currency units; annual pass 100; each visit incurs a 2-unit screening royalty. Some screenings sold out but the times were not recorded. A volunteer survey suggests pass holders bring friends. Capacity is uneven across nights and programming changed monthly. Analyze what can and cannot be inferred from this pilot. The board needs a proposal for the next season.

Write an original short story for an adult literary magazine's issue on borrowed things. A person who cuts keys for a living is asked to identify an unlabelled key after a neighborhood shop closes for good. The story takes place over one ordinary afternoon. Make the request matter to at least two people whose interests differ. The setting, characters, action, structure and ending are yours to invent. Submit the finished story, without an explanation or author bio.

Write an original short story for an adult literary magazine's issue on rehearsals. A local radio drama is rehearsing with a stand-in sound-effects operator when one familiar sound no longer works. An actor and the stand-in have different ideas about whether the audience will notice. Let the work of making radio shape the action. Invent your own cast, setting, structure and ending. Submit a finished story, without an explanation or author bio.
